extraction_warnings: This paper is a large-scale metagenomic assembly study aggregating 9,428 metagenomes from multiple studies. It does not present individual participant-level data suitable for sample-level extraction. Granularity is subgroup_level reflecting the four cohort categories (Madagascar, Ethiopia, Westernized public, Non-Westernized public).
Subject IDs and specific sample IDs are not provided in the paper; only NCBI BioProject accessions and cohort-level aggregates are reported.
Individual participant ages are not provided; only age category frequencies are reported.
Public datasets (46 studies) show heterogeneous protocols and metadata that cannot be uniformly captured for individual fields; values marked as 'Various' or 'not_reported'.
The paper emphasizes lifestyle ('Westernized' vs 'non-Westernized') rather than clinical conditions as the primary stratification factor.
Control status is inferred as 'Study Control' for the Madagascar and Ethiopia cohorts based on description as 'healthy volunteers', but not explicitly stated.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 1 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Madagascar cohort', 'Ethiopia cohort', 'Public datasets - Westernized', 'Public datasets - Non-Westernized']; kept batch 0.

This is a microbiome genomics survey paper analyzing 9,428 metagenomes from diverse populations and body sites. Most fields in the schema relate to clinical/patient characteristics that are not the focus of this research. The paper focuses on reconstructing and cataloging microbial genomes rather than detailed human host phenotyping.

Age information is available only at the group level (newborns <1 year, children, school-age, adults 19-65 years, seniors >65 years) across 9,316 public metagenomes from 46 studies, not per-sample. Individual sample ages not provided in the text.

Madagascar and Ethiopia cohorts included in the study involve 'healthy volunteers' (112 from Madagascar, 5 from Ethiopia) but other cohorts are from public repositories and limited metadata on individual participants available in this paper.

This paper is a metagenomic study focused on microbial genome reconstruction and diversity catalog creation. It does not contain clinical data, biomarkers, disease outcomes, or performance status measures typical of clinical studies. Most schema fields are not applicable.
The 'feces_phenotype_value' field was populated with microbiome-related measurements rather than traditional phenotype data, as this is the closest relevant microbial information available.
No individual sample-level data is provided in the paper; all reported values are study-level aggregates or statistics.
Paper reports 46 samples marked as missing metadata for age category, which is noted in the Methods but not detailed elsewhere.
